cfgBuilding.description: Farms produce all of your Food. Food is consumed during construction, research and training. Food is also essential to sustain your troops, either at home or on an expedition. Upgrade your Farms to increase your Food production.
cfgBuilding.name: Farm
cfgBuilding.summary: Farms produce all of your Food. Food is consumed during construction, research and training. Food is also essential to sustain your troops, either at home or on an expedition.

cfgBuilding.description: Sawmills produce Wood which can be used in construction, research and the manufacturing of weapons for your troops. Upgrade your Sawmills to increase your Wood production.
cfgBuilding.name: Sawmill
cfgBuilding.summary: Sawmills produce Wood which can be used in construction, research and the manufacturing of weapons for your troops.

cfgBuilding.description: Quarries produce Stone which is essential for construction and research. It also serves as ammunition for your Trebuchets. Upgrade your Quarries to increase your Stone production.
cfgBuilding.name: Quarry
cfgBuilding.summary: Quarries produce Stone which is essential for construction and research.

cfgBuilding.description: Mines produce Iron that can be used for making weapons and armor as well as in construction and research. Upgrade your Mines to increase your Iron production.
cfgBuilding.name: Mine
cfgBuilding.summary: Mines produce Iron that can be used for making weapons and armor as well as in construction and research.

cfgBuilding.description: Houses provide your citizens with shelter. Upgrade your Houses to attract more people to settle in your city.
cfgBuilding.name: House
cfgBuilding.summary: Houses provide your citizens with shelter.

cfgBuilding.description: The Senate is the hub of the city. Here you can adjust the tax rate, pacify the public and collect resources. Upgrade your Senate to control more resource sites in the outer city and to increase your Silver capacity limit.
cfgBuilding.name: Senate
cfgBuilding.summary: The Senate is the hub of the city. Here you can adjust the tax rate and govern your people.

cfgBuilding.description: Research technologies at the Academy to improve your production, combat skills and construction. Only one technology can be researched at a time. When you control multiple cities, your Academies can share research, provided they’ve reached the required level. This avoids duplicating research.
cfgBuilding.name: Academy
cfgBuilding.summary: You can improve your production, construction and combat skills by researching technologies at the Academy.

cfgBuilding.description: You can dispatch troops, give orders, set strategies and check the status of your troops at the Muster Field. Upgrading your Muster Field allows you to dispatch more troops in higher numbers at the same time.
cfgBuilding.name: Muster Field
cfgBuilding.summary: You can dispatch troops, give orders, set strategies and check the status of your troops at the Muster Field.

cfgBuilding.description: Your troops are trained and housed in the Barracks. They can also be demobilized there. Increasing the level of your Barracks allows you to train more advanced troops and to add more training queues.
cfgBuilding.name: Barracks
cfgBuilding.summary: Troops can be trained or demobilized at the Barracks.

cfgBuilding.description: A popular gathering place for local people. Heroes can be found and recruited in the Tavern. Upgrade your Tavern and it will attract higher level Heroes in greater numbers.
cfgBuilding.name: Tavern
cfgBuilding.summary: A popular gathering place for local people. Heroes can be found and recruited in the Tavern.

cfgBuilding.description: The Villa serves as your Heroes' residence. There you can check their status, alter their strategies, reward them or even dismiss them. To recruit a Hero, there must be a vacancy for them at the Villa. Upgrade your Villa to increase the amount of Heroes you can recruit.
cfgBuilding.name: Villa
cfgBuilding.summary: The Villa serves as your Heroes' residence.

cfgBuilding.description: The Embassy is used for Alliance affairs. With a Level 1 Embassy, you can join an Alliance. With a Level 2 Embassy, you can create your own. Upgrade your Embassy to increase the number of allied troops that it can accommodate.
cfgBuilding.name: Embassy
cfgBuilding.summary: The Embassy is used for Alliance affairs.

cfgBuilding.description: At the Market, you can use Silver to trade resources and treasure with merchants and other players. Upgrade the level of your Market to perform more transactions simultaneously.
cfgBuilding.name: Market
cfgBuilding.summary: At the Market, you can use Silver to trade resources and treasure with merchants and other players.

cfgBuilding.description: Weapons are forged here by the blacksmith. You must build a Blacksmith's before you can raise a powerful army.
cfgBuilding.name: Blacksmith's
cfgBuilding.summary: Weapons are forged here by the blacksmith. You must build a Blacksmith's before you can raise a powerful army.

cfgBuilding.description: Fortifications, siege weapons and other machinery are made at the Workshop.
cfgBuilding.name: Workshop
cfgBuilding.summary: Fortifications, siege weapons and other machinery are made at the Workshop.

cfgBuilding.description: Horses are trained and housed in the Stable. You must build a Stable before you can start recruiting a cavalry.
cfgBuilding.name: Stable
cfgBuilding.summary: Horses are trained and housed in the Stable. You must build a Stable before you can start recruiting a cavalry.

cfgBuilding.description: Storehouses can protect Food, Stone, Wood and Iron from plunder. Upgrade your Storehouses to increase the amount of protected resources.
cfgBuilding.name: Storehouse
cfgBuilding.summary: Storehouses can protect Food, Stone, Wood and Iron from plunder.

cfgBuilding.description: Relay Stations can greatly increase the marching speed of your troops between your cities and those of your allies. Upgrade your Relay Stations to increase your army's marching speed.
cfgBuilding.name: Relay Station
cfgBuilding.summary: Relay Stations can greatly increase the marching speed of your troops between your cities and those of your allies.

cfgBuilding.description:
Watchtowers, built on high ground, can be 
used for long-range observation and can 
provide early warnings of enemy invasions. Upgrade the level of your Watchtower to receive more detailed warnings and intelligence.
cfgBuilding.name: Watchtower
cfgBuilding.summary: Watchtowers, built on high ground, can be used for long-range observation and can provide early warnings of enemy invasions.

cfgBuilding.description: A City Wall protects against invaders and Fortifications can be built along it. The Defense of all troops, and the range of long-range units, will be increased when stationed within the City Wall. Upgrading your City Wall allows for more types of Fortifications to be built in greater numbers.
cfgBuilding.name: City Wall
cfgBuilding.summary: A City Wall provides protection against invaders. Many types of Fortifications can be built atop your City Wall.

cfgDefence.description: Spike Traps are effective against any type of enemy unit. Spike Traps are consumable items.
cfgDefence.name: Spike Trap

cfgDefence.description: Barricades are sharp, wooden poles arranged into tight groups. They can inflict massive damage to fast-moving enemy units.
cfgDefence.name: Barricade

cfgDefence.description: Archer Towers built atop the City Wall provide your Archers with excellent vantage points for firing at the enemy.
cfgDefence.name: Archer Tower

cfgDefence.description: Falling Logs are a devastating defensive weapon and they can kill enemy troops in large numbers. Falling Logs are consumable items.
cfgDefence.name: Falling Logs

cfgDefence.description: Boulders are very effective against enemy siege weapons. They are consumable items.
cfgDefence.name: Boulder

cfgSoldier.description: Peasants can transport resources and weaponry. They have barely any combat skills.
cfgSoldier.name: Peasant

cfgSoldier.description: Auxiliaries can be recruited and trained in large numbers for a small cost. They have only basic training and few combat skills.
cfgSoldier.name: Auxiliary

cfgSoldier.description: Scouts are trained with espionage skills. They move swiftly to infiltrate enemy cities to spy for intelligence. The more Scouts you send, the more detailed information you will receive.
cfgSoldier.name: Scout

cfgSoldier.description: Pikemen are highly effective against enemy cavalry. Their long pikes strike fear into the hearts of enemy horsemen.
cfgSoldier.name: Pikeman

cfgSoldier.description: Legionaries are equipped with swords and shields. They are effective against Archers as their shields offer good protection.
cfgSoldier.name: Legionary

cfgSoldier.description: Archers provide an excellent long-distance attacking option but they are vulnerable at close range.
cfgSoldier.name: Archer

cfgSoldier.description: Fast and responsive, the horsemen of the Light Cavalry are the ideal troops for raiding and plundering.
cfgSoldier.name: Light Cavalry

cfgSoldier.description: Heavily armored horsemen are a devastating weapon on the battlefield. They can attack and defend with equal skill.
cfgSoldier.name: Armored Cavalry

cfgSoldier.description: These wagons move slowly but they can carry huge amounts of resources. Their crews have almost no combat skills.
cfgSoldier.name: Transport Wagon

cfgSoldier.description: Ballistae can fire penetrating shots from long range. They can inflict huge damage on defensive weapons and positions. However, they are heavy and slow and therefore vulnerable to attacks at close range.
cfgSoldier.name: Ballista

cfgSoldier.description: Battering Rams can wreak havoc on an enemy's fortifications and defenses. However, due to their size, they can only move slowly.
cfgSoldier.name: Battering Ram

cfgSoldier.description: Trebuchets can fire boulders and other projectiles at your enemy's city, damaging fortifications and defenses. They take time to move, however, and so they are vulnerable to attack by enemy cavalry.
cfgSoldier.name: Trebuchet

Can reduce 70 points morale maximum.Thisstrategy will not be effective on the same enemy if used again within 24 hours
cfgTrick.manual: This strategy can only be used on an enemy city.
cfgTrick.name: Demoralize

cfgTrick.description: After using this strategy, the loyalty of one of your enemy's Heroes will be reduced. For every 10 Wisdom points your Hero has, enemy loyalty will be reduced by 1 point. The lowest it can reduced to is 0. This strategy will not be effective on the same Hero if used again within 24 hours.
cfgTrick.manual: This strategy can only be used on an enemy city.
cfgTrick.name: Seeds of Dissent

cfgTrick.description: After using this strategy, you will immediately enter a state of war with the target. For every 1 Wisdom point your Hero has, the effect will last for 1 minute. At the same time, your Prestige will reduced. This strategy will not be effective on the same enemy if used again within 6 hours.
cfgTrick.manual: This strategy can only be used on an enemy city.
cfgTrick.name: Surprise Attack

cfgTrick.description: By successfully trapping an enemy army, marching time will be extended and the army cannot be recalled until the end of the attack. The extension in time will be determined by their hero wisdom, with every ten hero wisdom points equating to another minute of marching time. The army can then not be trapped for six hours.
cfgTrick.manual: This strategy can be used in Enemy Alert.
cfgTrick.name: Ambush

cfgTrick.description: This strategy will speed up your troops' progress and reduce their marching time. For every 1 Wisdom point your Hero has, the troops' marching speed will be increased by 2%. This strategy can't be used on the same troops again within 1 hour.
cfgTrick.manual: You can implement this Strategy on the Troop Details menu when your troops are marching.

cfgTrick.description: Each time you successfully occupy a city, the Morale of the people will decline by 5. For 1 Wisdom point, the effect will be sustained for 1 minute. This won't be effective on the same target again for 6 hours.
cfgTrick.manual: This Strategy can only be used against County Cities and normal NPC cities.
cfgTrick.name: Morale Crusher

cfgTrick.description: Each time you successfully occupy a city, the Discontent of the people will increase by 20. For 1 Wisdom point, the effect will be sustained for 1 minute. This won't be effective on the same target again for 6 hours.
cfgTrick.manual: This Strategy can only be used against County Cities and normal NPC cities.
cfgTrick.name: Spark of Discontent

cfgTrick.description:
Once successful, your enemy will be unable to call in allied reinforcements to the city. The duration of this is determined by the difference between the heroes' wisdom, with every two points of difference equating to one minute. As well as this, the city cannot be trapped again for another 24 hours.
* reinforcements already present in the city will not be affected
* reinforcements who have already gone into battle will be not be affected
cfgTrick.manual: Strategies should only be used against enemy cities.

This will not effect the same target again for another 8 hours
cfgTrick.manual: This scheme can only be used on enemis of the city.

*The same effects will not stack.

cfgTrick.description: After use, each Wildland you occupy (up to a maximum effective number of 10% of your Strategy) will provide your troops with a 0.5% Increase Hurt and reduce enemy troop's Wounded rate by 0.2%. This strategy will not be effective if used again
cfgTrick.manual: You can implement this Strategy on the Troop Details menu when your troops are marching.
cfgTrick.name: Wildland Lord

cfgTrick.description:
When used, your next battle within 12 hours will grant your troops +15% Speed and increase enemy death rate by 5%. For every 100 points of the Official’s Intelligence, each effect is increased by an additional 1%. Can be used once every 48 hours.
*The effect applies to all cities, not just the current one.
cfgTrick.manual: This scheme can only be used on the city your troops currently occupy.
cfgTrick.name: Master Mind

cfgTrick.description: During this battle, all enemy ranged troops are forced to advance for 4 rounds. This strategy will not be effective if used again.
cfgTrick.manual: You can implement this Strategy on the Troop Details menu when your troops are marching.
cfgTrick.name: Promise
